title: Budgets and prices
request: Add money to the gateway: price each request from one dated table, enforce per-run, per-project and per-workspace caps before a request is sent, and show real spend on the Compute and Admin pages. Never guess a price.
spec: One price table (euros per million tokens, with a date); caps per project per run, per project per month and per workspace per month; the wizard's euro budget becomes a real cap; a refusal says how much is left; spend from the usage table on Compute and Admin; 'not metered' removed only where it is now true; an unknown model is 'price not configured' and counted in tokens only. Done when a scripted run over its cap is refused before the request is sent and the pages show euros from the usage table.
plan: Write dclab_rnd/models/prices.py (or DCLAB_PRICES_FILE) with a date per table; a model without a price is counted in tokens only; a request to a model on this machine is free.
Add the cost to the usage log (migration 0003) and the caps to the gateway: the intern session's max_eur (run), the wizard's budget (project, per month), DCLAB_WORKSPACE_MONTHLY_EUR (workspace).
Show the euros on Compute and Admin, and how many requests have no price.
Update the test that asserted spend is not tracked, since that is exactly what changed.
Run check-all and the review; fix the six findings with tests; render the two pages; commit.

decisions.decision: Refuse a request when its upper-bound cost could pass a cap, checked and reserved under a lock.
decisions.why: Checking 'already over' lets the request that crosses the cap through, and an unlocked check lets concurrent requests near the cap all pass.

decisions.decision: The upper bound is the prompt's characters divided by three times the input price plus max_tokens times the output price.
decisions.why: The real token count is known only after the reply; an estimate that is never lower than the truth keeps the cap a cap.

decisions.decision: Never guess a price; an unpriced model is counted in tokens.
decisions.why: A guessed price would make a cap look enforced while it is not; showing 'no price' tells the owner what to configure.

change: dclab_rnd/models/prices.py (dated table or DCLAB_PRICES_FILE), cost per request in the usage log (migration 0003), caps in the gateway (run, project per month, workspace per month), the intern's max_eur budget, spend in euros on the Compute and Admin pages.

findings.defect: An intern session's euro cap restarted from zero on every message.
findings.scenario: A session with max_eur=1 spends 1 euro and is refused; POST /message gives it another euro, and again, with no limit. A server restart does the same.
findings.cause: The server builds a new Intern and a new bound client for each start or message, and a new bound client starts with spent_eur=0.
findings.fix: The session keeps its spend in session['used']['eur']; the loop loads it into the client before each request and writes it back afterwards.
findings.test: A test of a session refused at its cap that stays refused after a follow-up.

findings.defect: A malformed price file lost an answer that had already been paid for.
findings.scenario: DCLAB_PRICES_FILE holds a model price without as_of: the request is sent, then the cost computation raises KeyError; the answer is lost and no usage row is written.
findings.cause: The price was looked up after sending and outside the error handling.
findings.fix: The price table is loaded and checked before a request is sent; a broken table stops requests before they cost anything.
findings.test: A test with a malformed price file that sends nothing.

findings.defect: Research-campaign requests skipped the caps and were priced wrongly.
findings.scenario: The NOOA clients only record after a request, so DCLAB_WORKSPACE_MONTHLY_EUR never stops a campaign on the strong tier; NOOA names the model 'openai/<model>', so every price lookup misses; and 'local' was judged from the campaign tier's URL while litellm sends to OPENAI_BASE_URL, so remote calls could be logged as free.
findings.cause: The campaign adapters were wired for counting only, not for checking.
findings.fix: The campaign clients ask the gateway for a refusal before each request and raise if refused, and record the model name without the 'openai/' prefix.
findings.test: Campaign adapter tests with a cap reached.

findings.defect: 'Local' was a substring match, so a remote endpoint could be logged as free and never capped.
findings.scenario: https://api.example.com:11434/v1, https://localhost.example.com/v1 and a URL with '127.0.0.1' in its query were all judged local.
findings.cause: The check searched the URL text.
findings.fix: Local means the host is exactly localhost, 127.0.0.1 or ::1, or the tier says DCLAB_TIER_<T>_LOCAL=1.
findings.test: A settings test over the three misleading URLs.

findings.defect: The cap check was 'already over', not 'would pass', and had no lock.
findings.scenario: The request that crosses the cap was always sent (the test itself expected 3.60 euros spent of a 3.00 cap); the project message always said '0.00 left'; N concurrent requests near the cap were all sent.
findings.cause: The gateway compared spent with the cap before sending, without reserving anything.
findings.fix: Under a gateway lock, reserve an upper-bound estimate and refuse when spent plus the estimate is over the cap; report cap minus spent as what is left.
findings.test: The money tests were rewritten to the 'would pass' rule, with a concurrent case.

findings.defect: Bad max_eur values and a budget refusal were handled badly.
findings.scenario: max_eur 'nan' became 0.0 and 'abc' gave a 500; max_eur=0 refused even free local requests; a budget refusal ended the session as 'failed' with a RuntimeError, while the step and minute budgets end it as 'budget_exhausted' with a progress note.
findings.cause: No validation of the value, and the budget error was not caught in the loop.
findings.fix: Non-finite and non-numeric values are refused with a clear message; a zero cap refuses only priced requests; the loop catches the budget error and ends the session as budget used up.
findings.test: Intern tests for each value and for the session's end state.

findings.defect: A test claimed to check a free local model under a zero cap but did not exercise that path.
findings.scenario: The test passed whether or not local requests were exempt.
findings.cause: The scripted endpoint was not marked local.
findings.fix: The test now uses a local tier and asserts the request is sent at zero cost.

outcome: Done: costs come from a dated price table, a request whose upper-bound cost could pass a run, project or workspace cap is refused before it is sent, under a lock, and Compute and Admin show euros. Open: no price is configured yet, so remote requests are counted in tokens until prices are added. The gate passed with 379 tests on each backend and the four flows.
lessons: A cap must be checked against what the request could cost, before sending and under a lock; 'already over' always lets one request through.
Anything computed after a paid request must not be able to lose its answer.
Decide 'local' from the parsed host, never from a substring of the URL.
